newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OSCE mission head must leave - Chechnya officials.
newsitem.headline: OSCE mission head must leave - Chechnya officials.

text.p: Chechen authorities said on Tuesday they had ordered the head of mission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to leave, criticising him for calling Chechnya part of the Russian Federation.

"The Foreign Ministry of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria considers the further presence of (Tim) Guldimann on the territory of Chechnya to be inadmissible," the self-styled foreign ministry said in a statement.

The document was distributed by the press secretary of current President Zelimkhan Yandabiyev, who leaves office next week after having lost the January 27 presidential election in the first round to Aslan Maskhadov.

Guldimann could not be reached for comment, although Russian Public Television said he would comment once outside Chechnya. According to a member of the presidential guard, he was ordered to leave Chechnya by 5:30 p.m. (1430 GMT).
Four cars from the presidential guard were seen leaving the OSCE compound at about 5 p.m.

Guldimann, a Swiss diplomat, declared the January 27 presidential election in Chechnya free and fair. But in their statement Chechen authorities criticised remarks Guldimann made at a news conference last week. "During this press conference, Mr. Guldimann stated that the OSCE considers the Chechen republic of Ichkeria a part of the Russian Federation," it said.
